claim: Listeria monocytogenes is a food-borne pathogen and the causative agent of listeriosis with a mortality of 20–30%.
source: Listeria monocytogenes (Lm) is a food-borne pathogen and the causative agent of listeriosis, a severe human illness that is acquired upon eating contaminated food with a mortality of 20–30% (Bucur et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citation to Bucur et al., 2018

claim: Listeria monocytogenes cannot grow at temperatures above 45°C.
source: While Lm can efficiently persist in food-producing plants, it cannot grow at temperatures above 45°C, qualifying heat treatments as efficient possibility to eradicate the pathogen.
evidence: Stated as established knowledge about Lm growth characteristics

claim: Listeria monocytogenes strains showing up to 1000-fold enhanced heat resistance have been described.
source: However, Lm strains that show an up to 1000-fold enhanced heat resistance have been described (Lundén et al., 2008).
evidence: Supported by citation to Lundén et al., 2008

claim: Environmental and food-related Lm strains frequently harbor plasmids encoding protection factors against various stresses including heat.
source: Environmental and food-related Lm strains frequently harbor plasmids that encode for open reading frames providing protection against antibiotics, disinfectants, heavy metals, high salt concentrations, low pH, and heat stress (Jiang et al., 2016; Lebrun et al., 1994; Naditz et al., 2019; Pöntinen et al., 2017; Poyart-Salmeron et al., 1990).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations

claim: Heat resistance at 55°C is provided by the chaperone ClpL, which is encoded on diverse Lm plasmids.
source: Heat resistance at 55°C is provided by the chaperone ClpL, which is encoded on diverse Lm plasmids (Pöntinen et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citation to Pöntinen et al., 2017

claim: ClpL presence does not increase the maximum growth temperature of Lm but strongly enhances cell survival upon sudden exposure to extreme temperatures.
source: ClpL presence does not increase the maximum growth temperature of Lm but strongly enhances cell survival upon sudden exposure to extreme temperatures.
evidence: Stated as established knowledge about ClpL function

claim: ClpL is encoded in the core genome of various Gram-positive bacteria including Staphylococcus aureus and Streptococcus pneumoniae.
source: ClpL is also encoded in the core genome of various Gram-positive bacteria including the major pathogens Staphylococcus aureus and Streptococcus pneumoniae.
evidence: Stated as established knowledge about ClpL distribution

claim: clpL gene expression is typically upregulated upon heat shock.
source: clpL gene expression is typically upregulated upon heat shock and clpL knockout strains can exhibit increased sensitivity to heat stress, suggesting a function of ClpL in cellular proteostasis (Li et al., 2011; Suokko et al., 2008; Suokko et al., 2005).
evidence: Supported by citations to Li et al., 2011; Suokko et al., 2008; Suokko et al., 2005

claim: clpL knockout strains can exhibit increased sensitivity to heat stress.
source: clpL gene expression is typically upregulated upon heat shock and clpL knockout strains can exhibit increased sensitivity to heat stress, suggesting a function of ClpL in cellular proteostasis (Li et al., 2011; Suokko et al., 2008; Suokko et al., 2005).
evidence: Supported by citations to Li et al., 2011; Suokko et al., 2008; Suokko et al., 2005

claim: ClpL belongs to the AAA+ (ATPase associated with diverse cellular activities) protein family.
source: ClpL belongs to the AAA+ (ATPase associated with diverse cellular activities) protein family.

source: AAA+ proteins typically form hexameric assemblies and thread substrates through an inner channel under consumption of ATP.

claim: The specific role ClpL plays in bacterial proteostasis remained undefined prior to this study.

claim: Severe heat shock triggers massive protein aggregation, titrating crucial components of essential cellular processes including transcription, translation, and cell division.
source: Severe heat shock triggers massive protein aggregation, titrating crucial components of essential cellular processes including transcription, translation, and cell division.

claim: Selected Gram-negative bacteria including Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Klebsiella pneumoniae adapt to man-made stress regimes by acquiring the autonomous AAA+ ClpG disaggregase, which confers extreme heat resistance.

Selected Gram-negative bacteria including major pathogens like Pseudomonas aeruginosa (Pa) or Klebsiella pneumoniae adapt to these man-made stress regimes by acquiring the autonomous AAA+ ClpG disaggregase, which confers extreme heat resistance (Bojer et al., 2010; Boll et al., 2017; Lee et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citations to Bojer et al., 2010; Boll et al., 2017; Lee et al., 2018

claim: clpG is encoded on plasmids or mobile genomic islands (transmissible locus of stress resistance [tLST]) together with other open reading frames linked to protein quality control.

source: ClpL showed substantial disaggregation activity toward heat-aggregated luciferase that was 0.67-fold (p=1.9e-16) reduced as compared to ClpG, but 3.1-fold higher as compared to the Lm Hsp70 (KJE)-ClpB bi-chaperone disaggregase (p=1e-23), which we included as references (Figure 1B).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B with statistical analysis

claim: Addition of Lm KJE to ClpL did not significantly enhance ClpL disaggregation activity when monitored directly by turbidity measurements.
source: Addition of Lm KJE to ClpL increased the reactivation of aggregated luciferase 1.7-fold (p=1.7e-18), however, it did not significantly enhance ClpL disaggregation activity (p1xKJE = 0.19, p2xKJE = 0.19) when monitored directly by turbidity measurements (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B/C).

claim: The formation of ring dimers is observed for other AAA+ family members.
source: The formation of ring dimers is also observed for other AAA+ family members and their functional roles are currently actively discussed.
evidence: Stated as established knowledge

claim: p97 double rings form by ATPase ring interactions and are suggested to represent a potentiated state.
source: p97 double rings form by ATPase ring interactions and are suggested to represent a potentiated state (Gao et al., 2022).
evidence: Supported by citation to Gao et al., 2022

claim: Dodecamers of the bacterial AAA+ protease Lon regulate substrate selectivity and mostly exhibit reduced proteolytic activity.
source: Dodecamers of the bacterial AAA+ protease Lon regulate substrate selectivity and mostly exhibit reduced proteolytic activity (Vieux et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citation to Vieux et al., 2013

claim: The role of ring dimers of the human mitochondrial disaggregase Skd3 in protein disaggregation is controversial.
source: The role of ring dimers of the human mitochondrial disaggregase Skd3 in protein disaggregation is controversial and both higher and lower disaggregation activity has been associated with this state (Cupo et al., 2022; Gupta et al., 2023; Lee et al., 2023; Spaulding et al., 2022; Wu et al., 2023).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations showing conflicting results

claim: ClpL ring assemblies might represent storage states, reducing ClpL activity by shielding NTDs.
source: We speculate that they might represent storage states, reducing ClpL activity by shielding NTDs.
evidence: Speculation based on experimental findings

claim: ClpL ring assemblies have a physiological role in controlling ClpL activity.
source: We observed toxicity upon production of ClpL MD mutants in Ec cells, pointing to a physiological role of ClpL ring assemblies in controlling ClpL activity.
evidence: Inference based on experimental data showing toxicity
